title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: admins create custom MCP connectors in the admin centre
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents preview automation for the publisher-type and User access settings, so their API columns must not say Not yet documented. The roadmap facts, licensing, creation instructions and administrative paths are supported; a separate Learn overview still describes federated connectors as read-only and should be acknowledged.

claims.claim: Admins can create custom MCP connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin centre and deploy them across Microsoft 365 to surface organizational data in Copilot.
claims.quote: Admins can create custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectors in the Microsoft 365 Admin Centre and deploy them across Microsoft 365.

claims.quote:
go to Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access.
2. Clear the publisher types you want to block:

claims.fix: Replace controls[0].api null with kind graph, call 'POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors', docs https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/configurationmanagement-post-configurationmonitors?view=graph-rest-beta. Append to its note: 'Preview TCM automation uses mode=applyOnce and an inline baseline resource with resourceType=microsoft.agent.allowedagenttypes, resourceVersion=1 and properties.valueObject.areTenantScopedAppsAllowed=false to block organization-built items. Narrow the final Open question to 'Will Microsoft publish APIs for individual custom-connector staging and blocking?'

claims.claim: Clearing the organization-built publisher type sets existing custom connectors to No users while keeping them visible to admins.
claims.quote: When you clear an option, existing connectors of that type remain visible to admins in Copilot connectors > Your connections, but their staged rollout is set to No users.

claims.claim: An individual connector setting takes precedence over bulk Agent and plugin access.
claims.quote: A setting you make on an individual connector takes precedence over the bulk Agent and plugin access setting. User access always applies.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Custom federated connectors use an MCP server's exposed tools to access data in internal systems.
claims.quote: A custom federated connector starts with a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that exposes tools for Microsoft 365 Copilot to access data or take actions in your internal systems.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Where the MCP server exposes appropriate tools, the connector can create, update or delete data.
claims.quote: Where a connector provides the tools, Copilot can also create, update, or delete data in the connected system on the user's behalf.
claims.fix: Keep the write-capability statement, but add: 'Microsoft Learn is inconsistent: the general Copilot connectors overview still calls federated connectors read-only, while the dedicated federated connectors overview documents create, update and delete tools.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview#types-of-copilot-connectors, whose search excerpt states 'Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.'

claims.claim: Creating a connector takes a display name, description and MCP server base URL.
claims.quote:
Display name | The user-facing name for your connector.
Description | A summary of your data source and the information it provides.
Base URL | Your MCP server endpoint.

claims.quote: The source system enforces all permissions. Users can only access content they're authorized to view and make changes they're authorized to make in the original data source.

claims.quote: Data processed by non-Microsoft services isn't subject to Microsoft agreements.

claims.claim: An MCP server restricting source IP addresses needs Microsoft's static egress addresses allowed.

claims.claim: Static egress is enabled by default.
claims.quote: Static egress is enabled by default; no manifest flag is required.

claims.where: Governance controls; summary; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Publisher access, User access and connector staging must all allow the user, subject to individual connector overrides of publisher access.
claims.quote: All of them must allow the user. Agent and plugin access decides whether a connector type is available; a connector you turn on individually overrides it. User access sets the maximum population. Staged rollout narrows access within that population.

claims.claim: A non-admin test user can check effective connector availability in Copilot Chat > Settings > Sources.
claims.quote: Then sign in as a test user who isn't an admin, open Copilot Chat > Settings > Sources, and confirm the connector isn't listed.

claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval. Admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview.
